preamble: Close-mid [o] is lowered to open-mid [ɔ] as a positional allophone, typically in closed syllables. In Javanese /o/ is [ɔ] in closed syllables and in an open syllable followed by an open syllable with i or u (kori [kɔri] 'gate'), but [o] elsewhere (loro [loro] 'two'). In Faroese the long vowel [oː] alternates with short [ɔ] before consonant clusters (tola [ˈtʰoːla] 'to endure', toldi [ˈtʰɔltɪ] 'endured').

examples.note: The closed final syllable has [ɔ]; compare loro [loro] 'two', with [o] in open syllables.

languageExamples.context: Closed syllables, and open syllables before an open syllable with i or u

examples.note: Compare tola [ˈtʰoːla ~ ˈtʰoɔːla] 'to endure' with long [oː].
Wiktionary transcribes this word phonemically with /ɔ/, treating short [ɔ] as a separate phoneme; the Wikipedia alternation table treats it as the short variant of /o/.
